Dear Sir,

I accuse receipt of your correspondence dated 27 November 1992 and, motivated by its contents, I respond to your request at this time.

As the current head of the Major Command of the General Air Command (COMGAR), I pass on the attached documentation prepared by our working group for the NuCOMDABRA, in order to complete the archive of this specific section of that Command.

In conclusion, I congratulate the entire GT for their meticulous work. From the context, the references to my Force, attributed in an unjust manner, reveal nothing about the matter.

Regarding the Air Defense, its purpose is, in principle, to control the airspace safely and in real time. The occurrences of phenomena and the reports under discussion are difficult to clarify, since, generally, they are reported after the fact, with very few elements that can help in a more accurate evaluation.

Wishing you much success in the endeavors for 1993, I sign off.

Dear Sirs:

At (pre-dawn - current time 05:00) on March 15th, 1993, I (a witness) observed an unusual phenomenon in the northern sky. It started as a single point of light, comparable to a star, but soon evolved into a larger object. This object appeared to be at a much lower altitude than any known satellite or current space debris, moving at a great velocity. Within 30 seconds, two additional aerial objects of similar size appeared, moving in the same direction as the first.

They seemed to be 2 or 3 in number, exactly positioned. Precisely, they were observed as "ant-like objects" passing by. We could clearly see them as aeroplanes with unusual wing patterns.

I might have mistaken it for an "upper-level object" due to the right-hand movement, following a straight path. There was no further activity after these three objects.

This phenomenon could have been a major sign, despite the fact that it might have been some kind of aircraft or unusual weather phenomenon. However, considering the clear and open sky, it could be something more significant.

I leave this testimony, hoping it might be of some use.
